digest:
## 🔬 Major Technical Developments

### Liquid AI reveals 8B-A1B MoE trained on 38T
URL: https://www.liquid.ai/blog/lfm2-5-8b-a1b
Mixture-of-experts architecture hits new efficiency benchmark at 8B parameters with 1B active.
Liquid's new model trained on 38 trillion tokens represents a significant push toward smaller, more efficient architectures that could run on edge devices. The 8:1 total-to-active parameter ratio signals where inference economics are heading — expect this pattern to proliferate as companies optimize for deployment cost over raw capability.

### Tiny-vLLM – high performance LLM inference engine in C++ and CUDA
URL: https://github.com/jmaczan/tiny-vllm
Open-source inference optimization is fragmenting the serving stack.
Another entrant in the crowded inference engine space, but the proliferation of these tools indicates that LLM serving infrastructure remains unsettled. Companies building on vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, or proprietary stacks should monitor — the winner here will shape deployment economics for years.

### This chip startup just raised $135M on a bet that AI's biggest bottleneck isn't compute — it's memory
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/29/xcena-secures-135m-at-570m-valuation-betting-on-memory-as-ais-real-bottleneck/
XCENA's $570M valuation bets memory bandwidth kills model scaling before compute does.
South Korean startup's thesis aligns with what we're seeing in transformer architecture constraints. HBM supply remains tight, SK Hynix and Micron can't meet demand, and memory-compute co-location is becoming the new battleground. Watch Samsung's response.

## 💼 Business & Market Signals

### SpaceX awarded $6.45B in Space Force contracts ahead of IPO
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/29/spacex-awarded-6-45b-in-space-force-contracts-ahead-of-ipo/
Government revenue concentration intensifies as IPO approaches.
With government contracts already comprising 20% of 2025 revenue, this $6.45B award further de-risks the revenue base for public market investors. Defense dependency cuts both ways — stable but politically exposed. Blue Origin's New Glenn explosion this week widens SpaceX's competitive moat.

### Glean's top line crosses $300M as AI budget cutting becomes its major selling point
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/28/gleans-top-line-crosses-300m-as-ai-budget-cutting-becomes-its-major-selling-point/
Enterprise AI search tripled revenue despite Google and Microsoft entering the category.
Glean's 3x growth trajectory while competing against bundled offerings from hyperscalers suggests enterprise buyers are willing to pay for best-of-breed AI tooling. The pivot to "budget cutting" positioning is notable — AI ROI narratives are maturing from productivity gains to cost reduction.

### After Nvidia's $20B not-acqui-hire, AI chip startup Groq reportedly raising $650M
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/29/after-nvidias-20b-not-acqui-hire-ai-chip-startup-groq-reportedly-raising-650m/
Groq pivots from hardware to inference services after Nvidia circled.
The $20B near-miss with Nvidia and now a $650M raise signals Groq sees more value in inference-as-a-service than chip manufacturing. Hardware commoditization thesis in action — the real margin may be in the serving layer, not silicon.

## 📋 Case Studies & Deep Dives

### SQLite is all you need for durable workflows
URL: https://obeli.sk/blog/sqlite-is-all-you-need-for-durable-workflows/
Single-file database as workflow engine challenges the Temporal/Inngest complexity stack.
Counternarrative to the distributed systems orthodoxy. For the 90% of companies who don't need planet-scale orchestration, SQLite's ACID guarantees and zero-ops deployment offer compelling economics. Watch for this pattern in AI agent architectures where workflow durability is critical.

### Shift will clean homes for free to train future robots
URL: https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/939765/ai-training-data-startup-shift-free-cleaning
Robotics startup offers free labor to capture manipulation training data.
Brilliant arbitrage: the cost of human cleaning is negative when that data trains household robots. This model inverts traditional data labeling economics. If Shift achieves sufficient demonstrations, they'll own a defensible dataset for the largest TAM in robotics — domestic automation.

### The Last Technical Interview
URL: https://steve-yegge.medium.com/the-last-technical-interview-bc13ddcf4564
Yegge declares traditional coding interviews obsolete in the AI era.
From the engineer who shaped Google's hiring practices, this is a directional signal. If senior technologists are abandoning whiteboard interviews, hiring infrastructure companies (HackerRank, Karat) face existential product questions. The new evaluation surface is unclear, creating opportunity.

## ⚡ Signal vs. Noise

The week's dominant thread is AI infrastructure fragmentation — inference engines, memory architectures, workflow durability, and evaluation systems are all being contested simultaneously. The "AI is dead" hot takes (MCP, frontend's lost decade) are noise; the signal is that every layer of the stack is being re-evaluated for AI-native design. Capital is flowing to picks-and-shovels plays that solve deployment economics rather than capability frontiers. Watch the memory bandwidth constraint — XCENA's raise and Groq's pivot both point to the same bottleneck.
